rows.title: Xcel’s grid, facing growing power demands, to get help from a bill racing through the legislature
rows.standfirst: The legislation would enable the utility to boost investment in its distribution grid to meet growth in rooftop solar, EVs and building electrification

rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado Springs’ weaker job market hasn’t slowed economic development wins
rows.standfirst: Officials aren’t too concerned yet. But high interest rates may be finally having an impact. Plus: Latest Colorado Springs expansions, layoffs and more.

rows.title: Colorado lawmakers reject push to prevent local short-term rental rules from applying to backcountry huts and cabins
rows.standfirst: Senate Bill 213, which was connected to the wealthy owner of a backcountry property outside Crested Butte, drew the ire of counties

rows.title: Effort to limit lawsuits over construction errors — and in turn boost Colorado condo construction — fails at Capitol
rows.standfirst: Senate Bill 106 died in a House committee Friday evening after it became clear the measure didn’t have enough votes to pass and there was no path to compromise

rows.title: As new laws are proposed, Colorado companies share how they use AI to make business better
rows.standfirst: Local AI startups are using generative artificial intelligence to add features and automation to achieve what they never thought possible. Where do the guardrails go?

rows.title: Colorado lawmakers reach last-minute bipartisan property tax deal that averts cuts to K-12 funding
rows.standfirst: The measure comes with three days left in Colorado’s 2024 lawmaking term — the minimum amount of time it needs to pass — and comes after negotiations with Colorado Concern, a business group that was backing a bigger cut on the November ballot

rows.title: Lawsuit by unhoused Lafayette father over city’s lack of indoor shelter dismissed
rows.standfirst: The claim that Lafayette ordinances preventing him from sleeping outdoors amount to cruel and unusual punishment was tossed just before U.S. Supreme Court took up a similar case.

rows.title: Meet Dr. Sammy, the Colorado researcher trying to fend off the next honeybee pandemic
rows.standfirst: As a new, virulent mite inches closer to North America, entomologist Sammy Ramsey’s work involves serious science and singing R&B to persuade Thai beekeepers to share their secrets

rows.title: Colorado lawmakers pass bipartisan property tax relief bill as 2024 legislative session comes to a close
rows.standfirst: The General Assembly hopes their legislation will persuade voters not to back property tax measures on the November ballot that would ravage state and local government budgets

rows.title: The six major Colorado land-use bills passed by Democrats in the legislature and aimed at housing affordability
rows.standfirst: The measures are aimed at making housing more affordable by increasing density and eliminating roadblocks to development

rows.title: Denver youth homeless shelter set to open in July scales back costs after losing wage dispute
rows.standfirst: Urban Peak, which is building a four-story, 136-bed shelter for young people ages 15-24, will have to pay an estimated $2 million in labor costs after losing its appeal

rows.title: 101 bills debated by the Colorado legislature in 2024 that you need to know about
rows.standfirst: The Colorado Sun pored through the more than 700 measures debated at the Capitol this year to highlight the most notable ones that passed and failed

rows.title: What’s Working: New Colorado laws that address the financial burden of growing older
rows.standfirst: Next50 and AARP find the highlights of how future laws could affect growing older in Colorado. Plus: Denver wages kept up with rent hikes better than most top metro areas.

rows.title: A broken bridge leaves an isolated Colorado community scrambling to save summer
rows.standfirst: Gunnison County residents have already felt the economic impacts from the U.S. 50 bridge closure over the Blue Mesa reservoir. Now a community reliant on summer tourism braces for more.

rows.title: Colorado receives $32.8 million to replace decades-old lead pipes and improve drinking water systems
rows.standfirst: Lead was once commonly used to build water service lines in communities because it was cheap and flexible but corrosion and high levels of it can cause serious health problems to children and adults

rows.title: Colorado EV sales dropped off by one measure, but green energy leaders say sky remains blue
rows.standfirst: Dealers worry about high loan costs, threats of Chinese imports and confusing rebates, but state says there’s no turning back

rows.title: Xcel may shut off power more often to avoid wildfires. Regulators have 8 questions about how that might work.
rows.standfirst: The state’s largest utility will file a new wildfire mitigation plan next month. The PUC would like it to include how “public safety” shutdowns can cause less pain for customers.

rows.title: Justice Department formally moves to reclassify marijuana as a less dangerous drug in historic shift
rows.standfirst: Plan approved by Attorney General Merrick Garland would not legalize marijuana outright for recreational use

rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado added a mere 300 jobs in April
rows.standfirst: But the housing market improved, at least in some areas. What’s going on with Colorado’s economy? It’s personal. Plus: Wages are up, tipping has increased and a new startup accelerator is coming to Greeley.

rows.title: Colorado becomes first state with law regulating potential consumer harms of artificial intelligence
rows.standfirst: Many in the technology industry said Senate Bill 205 is too broad. A task force is underway to guide the rollout of the law, which would go into effect February 2026.

rows.title: A workers’ co-op rises from the remains of a Colorado mushroom farm
rows.standfirst: Former Colorado Mushroom Farm workers use local backing to keep fungi fruiting in Alamosa

rows.title: Concentration of real estate agents in Colorado Springs is 3 times higher than the national rate
rows.standfirst: The local housing market had the worst April in years for homes sold. The number of real estate agents in the city is in decline. Those who remain stick with what works: cultivating relationships.

rows.title: At least 15 people died on Colorado slopes this ski season
rows.standfirst: All but one of the deaths that resulted from collisions and falls happened on intermediate or beginner slopes

rows.title: Big companies like to buy Colorado’s thriving outdoor businesses — and then move them out of state
rows.standfirst: As Colorado’s outdoor recreation industry matures and draws investment, part of that growth includes reshuffling, consolidation and new corporate strategies that can pull thriving businesses out of the state

rows.title: One lane of U.S. 50 could be open by July 4, but only if four critical repairs are completed on schedule
rows.standfirst: Travel will be limited to one direction at a time, a pattern familiar to people who have been stuck in stop-and-go construction traffic in Little Blue Canyon a few miles down the road for three years

rows.title: “Enormous progress” for tenants: Here’s how the Colorado legislature tried to help renters in 2024
rows.standfirst: Colorado’s Democratic majority secured a mix of major legislative wins and modest reforms that, taken together, amount to one of the largest policy packages aimed at renters in the state’s history

rows.title: “Shame on Polis”: Why the Colorado labor movement is so mad at the governor
rows.standfirst: Jared Polis vetoed six bills last week, three of which were priorities for state union leaders

rows.title: What’s Working: Nearly 55,000 Coloradans now have a retirement account after law went into effect
rows.standfirst: Colorado SecureSavings program, which launched last year, required employers to join if they didn’t offer a retirement plan. Many private employers ended up starting their own 401(k)s.

rows.title: 8 quirky places to visit in Colorado this summer for newbies and natives alike
rows.standfirst: Whether you live in Colorado or are just visiting, these quirky spots are just as engaging as some of the state’s better-known destinations

rows.title: Colorado is paying to house 100 former foster kids who left the system without a family
rows.standfirst: A new, $1 million housing voucher program is expected to pay at least 70% of rent for 100 young people each year who were in foster care at age 14 or older

rows.title: How much methane is Colorado’s oil and gas industry discharging? Regulators will soon start measuring.
rows.standfirst: Methane intensity will be measured across 12 Colorado counties as part of state requirements to significantly reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 2050

rows.title: Colorado’s nonlethal wolf deterrent methods aren’t working, ranchers say after seventh cow is killed
rows.standfirst: In April, officials gave Grand County ranchers $20,000 for a range rider to stop wolves from killing their calves. After another killing on May 11, ranchers are asking when parks and wildlife is going to do its job.

rows.title: Colorado bonding authority set to buy, develop the fabled Stanley Hotel in Estes Park after new law
rows.standfirst: Legislation signed by Gov. Jared Polis approves the Colorado Educational and Cultural Facilities Authority’s first-ever plan to acquire the Stanley Hotel and develop a new film center onsite

rows.title: Techstars new (and returning) CEO still calls Boulder home despite headquarters’ move to New York
rows.standfirst: The tech accelerator moved its headquarters to New York in February but after its New York CEO stepped down due to health problems, co-founder David Cohen takes over again

rows.title: One person killed in storm that flooded homes, stranded cars, damaged stores in Greeley
rows.standfirst: Many residents said they had to shovel drifts of heavy hail that was holding water in their yards and businesses

rows.title: Nearly two years since Colorado voters approved affordable housing measure, units are under construction in Denver
rows.standfirst: Construction of 102 apartments on West Colfax will begin next week. Two other complexes have broken ground, too. Proposition 123 was passed by Colorado voters in 2022.
